Absolute rules:

The prevalence of domestic and industrial electrical appliances has raised concerns about the health risk

[block=b00006 p.1 section=abstract chars=0:103]
of extremely low-frequency magnetic fields (ELF-MFs). At present, the effects of ELF-MFs on the central

[block=b00007 p.1 section=abstract chars=0:104]
nervous system are still highly controversial, and few studies have investigated its effects on cultured

[block=b00008 p.1 section=abstract chars=0:102]
neurons. Here, we evaluated the biological effects of different patterns of ELF-MF exposure on primary

[block=b00009 p.1 section=abstract chars=0:105]
cultured hippocampal neurons in terms of viability, apoptosis, genomic instability, and oxidative stress.

[block=b00010 p.1 section=abstract chars=0:103]
The results showed that repeated exposure to 50-Hz 2-mT ELF-MF for 8 h per day after different times in

[block=b00011 p.1 section=abstract chars=0:107]
culture decreased the viability and increased the production of intracellular reactive oxidative species in

[block=b00012 p.1 section=abstract chars=0:99]
hippocampal neurons. The mechanism was potentially related to the up-regulation of Nox2 expression.

[block=b00013 p.1 section=abstract chars=0:101]
Moreover, none of the repeated exposure patterns had significant effects on DNA damage, apoptosis, or

[block=b00014 p.1 section=abstract chars=0:97]
autophagy, which suggested that ELF-MF exposure has no severe biological consequences in cultured

[block=b00015 p.1 section=abstract chars=0:20]
hippocampal neurons.

[block=b00027 p.2 section=background chars=0:99]

[block=b00029 p.2 section=background chars=0:107]

[block=b00030 p.2 section=background chars=0:97]

[block=b00031 p.2 section=background chars=0:102]
